findings.name: “Not X but Y” (unqualified)
findings.why: The negation flip without a just/only/merely qualifier: “not a tool but a partner”. Slop Score weights this construction at 25% of its entire score, on its own, separate from word lists.
findings.suggest: Say what it is. The negated half is usually a straw man nobody proposed.
findings.sentence: Note that this is not a bug, but a feature — and it delves into the rich tapestry of data.

findings.name: Em dash
findings.why: An em dash, or an en dash or double hyphen standing in for one. Every occurrence, no threshold. This is a house-style rule and it is not optional: the owner of a document that carries it does not want em dashes in it.
findings.suggest: A comma if the aside is light, a colon if what follows explains, brackets if it is a true aside, a full stop if it is really a second sentence.
findings.sentence: Note that this is not a bug, but a feature — and it delves into the rich tapestry of data.

findings.name: AI vocabulary words
findings.why: Words LLMs lean on far more than people do: “delve”, “tapestry”, “meticulous”, “pivotal”, “intricate”, “interplay”, “underscore”, “garner”, “bolster”, “vibrant”, “bustling”, “multifaceted”, “seamless”, “ever-evolving”. One hit can be coincidence — several is a tell.
findings.suggest: Swap for a plainer word. One hit is coincidence; several is a tell.
findings.sentence: Note that this is not a bug, but a feature — and it delves into the rich tapestry of data.

findings.name: Promotional boilerplate
findings.why: Travel-brochure tone: “nestled in”, “in the heart of”, “rich tapestry / heritage”, “hidden gem”, “boasts a”, “breathtaking”, “stunning views”.
findings.suggest: Drop the brochure register and describe plainly.
findings.sentence: Note that this is not a bug, but a feature — and it delves into the rich tapestry of data.
